plain_text:
Being a caregiver or care partner is a big undertaking.
Caregivers don't just manage someone else's health care,
daily tasks, financial decisions, and other logistics. They also
have their own schedules and responsibilities to balance. It can be
hard to know where to begin!
semantic_text: Being a caregiver or care partner is a big undertaking. Caregivers don't just manage someone else's health care, daily tasks, financial decisions, and other logistics. They also have their own schedules and responsibilities to balance. It can be hard to know where to begin!

plain_text:
Whether you're new to caregiving or have been doing it for a while,
the National Institute on Aging's (NIA) website has expert-backed
advice to help make things more manageable. Here is just a sample
of what you'll find.
semantic_text: Whether you're new to caregiving or have been doing it for a while, the National Institute on Aging's (NIA) website has expert-backed advice to help make things more manageable. Here is just a sample of what you'll find.

plain_text:
As someone’s caregiver, it’s important to learn as much as possible
about their medical condition. This way you can better anticipate
their needs and how to manage their health care over time, including
in an emergency. Ask the person about what treatments they are
getting or medications they take. Get their health care providers’
contact information.
semantic_text: As someone’s caregiver, it’s important to learn as much as possible about their medical condition. This way you can better anticipate their needs and how to manage their health care over time, including in an emergency. Ask the person about what treatments they are getting or medications they take. Get their health care providers’ contact information.

plain_text:
If someone is hesitant to talk about their health with you, explain
that knowing this information will help you care for them. They may
prefer that you talk to their health care provider directly. Remember
that, by law, you need written permission from them to receive their
medical information unless they can give consent to the provider
in person.
semantic_text: If someone is hesitant to talk about their health with you, explain that knowing this information will help you care for them. They may prefer that you talk to their health care provider directly. Remember that, by law, you need written permission from them to receive their medical information unless they can give consent to the provider in person.

plain_text:
The Caregiver's Handbook is available to download online or order
for free. It outlines basic information on topics such as:
semantic_text: The Caregiver's Handbook is available to download online or order for free. It outlines basic information on topics such as:

plain_text:
■ Finding care needed at home
■ Long-term care facilities
■ The costs of caregiving
■ How to coordinate medical care
■ Planning ahead
■ Caring for yourself, too
semantic_text: ■ Finding care needed at home ■ Long-term care facilities ■ The costs of caregiving ■ How to coordinate medical care ■ Planning ahead ■ Caring for yourself, too

plain_text:
This guide is for anyone
who provides care for
family members or
friends who need help
with daily living.
semantic_text: This guide is for anyone who provides care for family members or friends who need help with daily living.

plain_text:
Hospitals, state and local governments, and nonprofit
organizations sometimes offer free or low-cost training for
caregivers. Check whether Medicare or Medicaid will cover
some of the cost, too!
semantic_text: Hospitals, state and local governments, and nonprofit organizations sometimes offer free or low-cost training for caregivers. Check whether Medicare or Medicaid will cover some of the cost, too!

plain_text:
Many caregivers help older adults and people with chronic health
conditions with mobility challenges. Physical activity is important
for just about everyone, including caregivers. Talk with the person's
health care provider about what's best and see whether there are any
exercises you two can do together.
semantic_text: Many caregivers help older adults and people with chronic health conditions with mobility challenges. Physical activity is important for just about everyone, including caregivers. Talk with the person's health care provider about what's best and see whether there are any exercises you two can do together.

plain_text:
Check out NIA's exercise ideas for someone with a chronic condition
such as:
semantic_text: Check out NIA's exercise ideas for someone with a chronic condition such as:

plain_text:
■ Alzheimer's disease and other dementias
■ Arthritis
■ Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
■ Type 2 diabetes
■ Heart health issues
■ Osteoporosis
■ Chronic pain
semantic_text: ■ Alzheimer's disease and other dementias ■ Arthritis ■ Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) ■ Type 2 diabetes ■ Heart health issues ■ Osteoporosis ■ Chronic pain

plain_text:
Caregiving involves keeping track of a lot of responsibilities and needs.
NIA has worksheets to help you remember everything and delegate
responsibilities to other family or friends when you need extra hands.
These worksheets include checklists about:
semantic_text: Caregiving involves keeping track of a lot of responsibilities and needs. NIA has worksheets to help you remember everything and delegate responsibilities to other family or friends when you need extra hands. These worksheets include checklists about:

plain_text:
■ Caregiver responsibilities
■ Medications and supplements
■ Important documents and paperwork
semantic_text: ■ Caregiver responsibilities ■ Medications and supplements ■ Important documents and paperwork

plain_text:
If you need to share caregiving responsibilities with others, think
about everyone's personal limits and who will be the best person for
each task.
semantic_text: If you need to share caregiving responsibilities with others, think about everyone's personal limits and who will be the best person for each task.

plain_text:
If someone is still living in their home while in your care, look for
potential falling hazards or areas where they may need extra help
to move around the house. NIA has a home safety checklist with
suggested precautions. You can also follow this room-by-room guide.
semantic_text: If someone is still living in their home while in your care, look for potential falling hazards or areas where they may need extra help to move around the house. NIA has a home safety checklist with suggested precautions. You can also follow this room-by-room guide.

plain_text: Other resources include:
semantic_text: Other resources include:

plain_text:
■ Advice for helping older adults avoid falls and fractures
■ Information on aging in place and knowing when it's time to
move somewhere more suitable
semantic_text: ■ Advice for helping older adults avoid falls and fractures ■ Information on aging in place and knowing when it's time to move somewhere more suitable

plain_text:
Your state or local government may have home modification
programs to help older people prevent falls. Ask your local health
department or Area Agency on Aging, or search the Eldercare
Locator.
semantic_text: Your state or local government may have home modification programs to help older people prevent falls. Ask your local health department or Area Agency on Aging, or search the Eldercare Locator.

plain_text:
Some nonprofit organizations and government agencies offer
services for older adults to help reduce some of the caregiving
workload. If an older adult needs help with daily needs, from chores
to grocery shopping to getting dressed, there may be a local service
to help with that.
